question: What are the benefits of using Next.js over a plain React app?
answerGeneral: Next.js adds what React deliberately leaves out: routing, server-side rendering, static generation, image and font optimisation, and a production build pipeline — all configured by convention rather than by hand. The three biggest wins over a plain SPA are SEO (the server sends real HTML instead of an empty shell), performance (less client JS, faster first paint), and developer ergonomics (file-based routing, no custom Webpack config, first-class TypeScript). The trade-off is adopting Vercel's conventions, but those conventions save weeks of setup on every new project.
answerPersonal: On the Butlin's booking site the migration from a custom Webpack SPA to Next.js wasn't just a DX win — the SSR and image optimisation defaults directly produced the LCP improvement from 4.8s to 2.5s that would have taken weeks of custom work to replicate in a plain React setup.
detailMd:
## What React leaves out React is a UI library, not a framework. It solves one problem — building component trees — and deliberately leaves everything else to you: - Routing — you pick React Router, TanStack Router, or something else - Data fetching — bring your own pattern - SSR / SSG — set up Node, Webpack, Babel, and wire it yourself - Image optimisation — manual srcset and lazy-loading - Code splitting — manual dynamic imports and chunk config - Build pipeline — configure Webpack or Vite from scratch Next.js makes all of those decisions for you, with sensible defaults you can override. ## The headline benefits ### 1. SEO — real HTML from the server A plain React SPA sends an empty `
`. Search engine crawlers see nothing to index: ```html
``` Next.js sends rendered HTML: ```html

Butlin's Skegness — Summer Breaks

From £299 per family...

``` Googles sees it. Social share previews see it. The page ranks. ### 2. Performance - **Route-level code splitting** — each page loads only its own JS - **next/image** — WebP, responsive srcsets, lazy loading, reserved space - **next/font** — self-hosted fonts with zero layout shift - **React Server Components** — component logic stays on the server, never ships to the browser - **Built-in caching** — pages served from the edge, not re-rendered per request ### 3. Developer ergonomics File-based routing removes the routing config entirely: ``` app/ ├── page.tsx → / ├── about/page.tsx → /about └── products/[id]/ └── page.tsx → /products/:id ``` No ``, no `createBrowserRouter`, no `path` strings. The folder is the route. TypeScript works out of the box. `tsconfig.json` is generated and kept in sync by Next.js. Framework types for layout props, page props, route handlers, and middleware are shipped in the package. ## When you might not need it - **Internal dashboards** that don't need SEO — a plain Vite/React app is simpler - **Design systems / Storybook** — no routing or SSR needed - **Static microsites** — Astro may be lighter For anything public-facing — marketing, e-commerce, SaaS, content sites — Next.js is the default for a reason.
answerGeneralTr: Next.js, React'in kasıtlı olarak dışarıda bıraktıklarını ekliyor: routing, server-side rendering, static generation, image ve font optimizasyonu ve bir production build pipeline — hepsi elle yapılandırma yerine convention ile. Düz bir SPA'ya göre üç büyük kazanım: SEO (server boş bir shell yerine gerçek HTML gönderiyor), performans (daha az client JS, daha hızlı first paint) ve developer ergonomisi (file-based routing, custom Webpack config yok, birinci sınıf TypeScript). Ödün Vercel'in convention'larını benimsemek, ama bu convention'lar her yeni projede haftalar kazandırıyor.
answerPersonalTr: Butlin's booking sitesinde custom Webpack SPA'dan Next.js'e geçiş sadece bir DX kazancı değildi — SSR ve image optimizasyonu default'ları, plain bir React setup'ta haftalar sürecek custom çalışmayla kopyalanabilecek LCP'yi 4.8s'den 2.5s'ye indirdi.

question: What is the Link component in Next.js and why use it instead of an anchor tag?
answerGeneral: next/link's Link component enables client-side navigation between pages without a full browser reload. Clicking it lets Next.js fetch only the data and JS for the destination route, preserving state and scroll in any persistent layouts. It also prefetches the linked page in the background when it appears in the viewport, so navigation feels instant. The rendered HTML is still a standard anchor tag for accessibility and SEO — Link just intercepts the click and hands it to the router.
answerGeneralTr: next/link'in Link component'i, tam tarayıcı yeniden yüklemesi olmadan sayfalar arasında client-side navigation sağlıyor. Tıklamak, Next.js'in yalnızca hedef route için data ve JS'i almasına izin veriyor; kalıcı layout'larda state ve scroll koruyor. Aynı zamanda viewport'ta göründüğünde bağlantılı sayfayı arka planda prefetch yapıyor, böylece navigasyon anında hissettiriyor. Render edilen HTML accessibility ve SEO için hâlâ standart bir anchor tag — Link sadece tıklamayı yakalayıp router'a veriyor.

question: How do you serve static files in Next.js?
answerGeneral: Files placed in the public/ folder at the project root are served as-is at the matching URL path. A file at public/logo.svg is accessible as /logo.svg — no import or build step needed. This is where favicons, robots.txt, open-graph images, and any asset that must live at a fixed URL belong. For images that benefit from lazy loading, responsive sizing, and format conversion, next/image is the better choice over dropping the file in public/ and using a plain img tag.
answerGeneralTr: Proje root'unda public/ klasörüne yerleştirilen dosyalar, eşleşen URL yolunda olduğu gibi servis ediliyor. public/logo.svg'deki bir dosyaya /logo.svg olarak erişilebiliyor — import veya build adımı gerekmiyor. Favicon, robots.txt, open-graph image'ları ve sabit bir URL'de bulunması gereken her asset buraya ait. Lazy loading, responsive boyutlandırma ve format dönüşümünden faydalanan image'lar için, dosyayı public/'a koyup plain bir img tag kullanmak yerine next/image daha iyi seçim.

question: What is Fast Refresh in Next.js and how does it work?
answerGeneral: Fast Refresh is the development hot-reload system built into Next.js. When you save a file, only the components affected by that change re-render — without losing their local state. If you edit a file that isn't a React component (a utility, a type, a constant), the relevant modules reload but the page keeps its state where possible. Syntax errors show an overlay with the exact location; fixing the error clears the overlay immediately, without a manual page refresh. It's powered by SWC's fast transform and React's hot-reload protocol.
detailMd: ## What it does Fast Refresh replaces the older hot module replacement (HMR) with a React-aware version that: 1. Rebuilds only the changed module (not the whole bundle) 2. Re-renders only the affected components 3. Preserves local `useState` and `useRef` values during the update 4. Shows an error overlay on syntax errors; clears it when the error is fixed ## Component edits — state preserved Edit a component's JSX or logic — the browser updates the component in place, keeping its state: ```tsx // You change this: export function Counter() { const [count, setCount] = useState(0); return ; } // To this: export function Counter() { const [count, setCount] = useState(0); return ( ); } ``` The count value in the running app is not reset to 0. The component re-renders with the new layout and the existing state intact. ## Module edits — state resets If you edit a non-component module (a utility function, a constant file), Fast Refresh reloads the module and re-renders the components that use it. State is reset in this case because the component tree has to re-mount from scratch when a non-component dependency changes. ## Error recovery ``` // You accidentally type: return
answerGeneralTr: Fast Refresh, Next.js'e yerleşik geliştirme hot-reload sistemi. Bir dosyayı kaydettiğinde, yalnızca bu değişiklikten etkilenen component'ler local state'lerini kaybetmeden yeniden render ediliyor. React component'i olmayan bir dosyayı (utility, type, sabit) düzenlersen, ilgili modüller yeniden yükleniyor ama mümkün olduğunda sayfa state'ini koruyor. Syntax hataları tam konumlu bir overlay gösteriyor; hatayı düzeltmek overlay'i anında temizliyor, manual sayfa yenilemesine gerek kalmıyor. SWC'nin hızlı transform'u ve React'in hot-reload protokolü ile güçlendirilmiş.

question: What built-in performance optimisations does Next.js provide?
answerGeneral: Next.js bundles several optimisations by default: automatic route-level code splitting so each page loads only its own JS; next/image for lazy loading, responsive srcsets, WebP/AVIF format conversion, and reserved space to prevent layout shift; next/font for self-hosted fonts with zero layout shift; next/script for controlled third-party script loading with priority strategies; and automatic prefetching of linked pages as they enter the viewport. On top of those, React Server Components remove entire component trees from the client bundle entirely — the biggest single lever for reducing JS payload.
answerPersonal: On Butlin's the most impactful quick wins were next/image with priority on the hero (killed the LCP delay), next/font replacing the third-party Google Fonts CDN request (cut a round trip), and moving the booking summary to a Server Component (stripped a chunk of client JS that was blocking hydration).
detailMd: ## Route-level code splitting Every page is its own JS chunk. The user visiting `/about` never downloads the JS for `/checkout`. This happens automatically — no dynamic import boilerplate needed for the pages themselves: ``` Route (app) Size First Load JS ┌ ○ / 2.1 kB 88 kB ├ ○ /about 1.4 kB 85 kB └ ƒ /checkout 4.2 kB 92 kB ``` The `First Load JS` column is what matters — shared framework code + this route's code. ## next/image ```tsx import Image from "next/image"; ``` What this buys you: - Lazy loading below the fold (scroll-triggered) - Responsive `srcset` — browser downloads the right size for the device - WebP / AVIF served when the browser supports it - Reserved space (prevents layout shift while the image loads) - On-demand resizing via the Image Optimisation API ## next/font ```tsx // app/layout.tsx import { Inter } from "next/font/google"; const inter = Inter({ subsets: ["latin"], display: "swap" }); export default function RootLayout({ children }) { return ( {children} ); } ``` Fonts are downloaded and self-hosted at build time. No round trip to Google's CDN at runtime, size-adjusted fallbacks eliminate CLS. ## next/script ```tsx import Script from "next/script"; // In a layout or page
answerGeneralTr: Next.js varsayılan olarak birçok optimizasyon birleştiriyor: her sayfanın yalnızca kendi JS'ini yüklemesi için otomatik route-level code splitting; lazy loading, responsive srcset, WebP/AVIF format dönüşümü ve layout shift'i önlemek için rezerve alan sağlayan next/image; sıfır layout shift ile self-hosted font'lar için next/font; öncelik stratejileriyle kontrollü üçüncü taraf script yükleme için next/script; ve viewport'a giren bağlantılı sayfaların otomatik prefetch'i. Bunların üstünde, React Server Components tüm component tree'lerini client bundle'dan tamamen çıkarıyor — JS payload'ını azaltmak için tek başına en büyük kaldıraç.
answerPersonalTr: Butlin's'te en etkili hızlı kazanımlar: hero'da priority'li next/image (LCP gecikmesini öldürdü), üçüncü taraf Google Fonts CDN isteğini kaldıran next/font (bir round trip'i kesti) ve booking summary'yi Server Component'e taşımak (hydration'ı bloke eden bir parça client JS'i söküp attı).

question: What is next.config.js and what can you configure in it?
answerGeneral: next.config.js (or next.config.ts) is the root-level configuration file for the Next.js build and dev server. Common uses are: defining allowed remote image domains via images.remotePatterns, setting up redirects and rewrites, enabling standalone output for Docker deployment, adding custom HTTP headers, turning on experimental features, extending the Webpack config, and setting the basePath or assetPrefix for CDN deployment. It runs in Node at build time, so you can read from process.env to keep secrets out of the file itself.
answerGeneralTr: next.config.js (veya next.config.ts), Next.js build ve dev server için root-level konfigürasyon dosyası. Yaygın kullanımlar: images.remotePatterns aracılığıyla izin verilen uzak image domain'lerini tanımlama, redirect ve rewrite kurma, Docker deployment için standalone output etkinleştirme, özel HTTP header ekleme, deneysel özellikler açma, Webpack config'i genişletme ve CDN deployment için basePath veya assetPrefix ayarlama. Build zamanında Node'da çalışıyor, dolayısıyla sırları dosyanın dışında tutmak için process.env'den okuyabilirsin.
